newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Ieng Sary says negotiates ceasefire with Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Ieng Sary says negotiates ceasefire with Cambodia.

text.p: Dissident Khmer Rouge leader Ieng Sary said on Monday he had negotiated a ceasefire with the Cambodian government, but more time and talks were needed for a comprehensive settlement.

"I would like to inform you that my talks for national reconciliation with the representatives from Phnom Penh were successful," he told more than 100 journalists at a news conference at his headquarters in this northwestern Cambodian town.
"We reached agreement on a ceasefire and to begin contact between our troops. They also agreed to provide legal protection for me," he added.

Ieng Sary, with several thousand followers, split from the Maoist Khmer Rouge's hardline leader Pol Pot last month. He held high-level peace talks with Cambodian co-defence ministers Tea Banh and Tea Chamrath in Bangkok last week.
"The question of disbanding of our troops and merging them with the government's is the most important issue and we are still in the process of negotiations on that subject," he said.

Ieng Sary was foreign minister during the Khmer Rouge rule in Cambodia during the late 1970s when more than one million people died from execution, starvation or disease in labour camps. He and Pol Pot were sentenced to death in absentia for their role in the genocide.
